publication_year_note: Published in International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction, Vol. 144 (2026), article 106311 (Received 23 February 2026; Revised 9 July 2026; Accepted 10 July 2026; Available online 14 July 2026).
rationale: Full text (17 pages) examined. Although described as a mixed-methods forensic disaster study, its quantitative component is strictly descriptive and deterministic rather than inferential. Specifically, the authors report: (1) Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI3, SPI6, SPI12) anomalies from ERA5 rainfall data (1991-2021); (2) descriptive monthly national load-shedding GWh and daily reservoir storage percentages; (3) municipal tanker/borehole counts and audit figures from secondary reports; and (4) a deterministic arithmetic indicator of per-capita water supply (dam storage multiplied by a 47% leakage estimate with a deterministic 30%-60% scenario band, divided by census population, falling from 106 to 15 L/capita/day). Governance, corruption, dual traditional/municipal authority, and emergency tanker failures are analysed qualitatively through 31 semi-structured interviews mapped onto a Pressure-and-Release (PAR) diagram and a qualitative Causal Loop Diagram (CLD). No inferential tests, regressions, correlations, standard errors, confidence intervals, or p-values appear anywhere in the paper.
